annotations.text: As shipped: two names and two sentences, then 600 points of nothing. The counts and the deploy key were removed on purpose (decision 63), but the page kept none of what the wire still offers.

A - Departures. Each row answers "if I press now, what do I land in?": the landing room's clock, the seats in the hangar's circle grammar (solid a person, ring a bot, dim nobody), friends on the row of their game, your Duel rung. Every fact is already in the directory reply the page asks for every three seconds. Costs: the busiest page of the three, and it half reverses the decision that stripped the counts.

B - Tuner. The room bleeding through the wash is the game under the cursor: resting on a row tunes the stands to it, so choosing a game is watching it, and the row carries one thin score line. Uses the delayed spectator feed that already exists; the page itself stays almost as bare as shipped. Costs: a channel change per hover, and a phone has no hover, so there it is first press tunes, second press joins, which bends "pressing a game means be in it".

C - Chart room. A game is a place: each card carries a chart of the ground the room is on now, drawn in the radar's own grammar, with the rotation's next ground and the spawn tiles in the side colors. Costs: the directory reply does not carry the map yet, so this is a wire change, and two cards spend most of the phone.
